findings.evidenceJa: 峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.explanation: 再来週 means the week after next, not next week. The English advances the university's incoming-student business by a full week in a scene whose calendar culminates in the February 14 scheduling conflict.
findings.japanese:
峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、
再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.todokanai: All of Houjou University's courses for this year will be finished by the end of the week. And the entrance exams for the new students will start next week.

findings.highlight: I'm finally done with my exams.
findings.explanation: The message says 'Good work on your exams,' not that the sender has finished hers. The following message separately says that Setsuna has just finished her last subject, so the English collapses two sides of the exchange and assigns the wrong content to this message.

findings.evidenceJa: ん～、全部の仕事が終わるまでには２月いっぱいかかるかなぁ
findings.explanation: 二月いっぱい means through the end of February. The scene is already in mid-February, so Mari expects roughly the rest of the month, not two whole months.
findings.japanese:
「ん～、全部の仕事が終わるまでには
２月いっぱいかかるかなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Hmm～ Wrapping up all my work is going to take two whole months, it seems."

findings.highlight: during her lunch break while she's at work on-site
findings.evidenceJa: 最近、麻理さんからは毎日『現地の』昼休みに電話がかかってくる。
findings.explanation: Quoted 現地の means Mari calls during the lunch hour in her local time abroad. The English reads 現地 as an on-site workplace, losing the time-zone contrast that establishes the daily international-call routine.
findings.japanese:
最近、麻理さんからは毎日
『現地の』昼休みに電話がかかってくる。
findings.todokanai: Nowadays, Mari-san calls me every day during her lunch break while she's at work on-site.

findings.highlight: She'll be continuing her business trip to America in December after that.
findings.evidenceJa: １２月に引き続きのアメリカ出張。しかも今度は、ほぼ一月間という長期滞在。
findings.explanation: Mari is on another American business trip following the one in December, and this time it is a nearly month-long stay. The English moves the trip into a future December and obscures that the present call is already coming from America.
findings.japanese:
１２月に引き続きのアメリカ出張。
しかも今度は、ほぼ一月間という長期滞在。
findings.todokanai: She'll be continuing her business trip to America in December after that. And I believe she's going to be staying there for about a month this time.

findings.evidenceJa: 「…好きですよ、麻理さんのこと」
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether Haruki 愛してくれてるか—whether he loves her—and he answers only 好きですよ, 'I do like/care for you.' The next narration explicitly says he still never reaches the words she truly wants. Translating his reply as 'I love you' erases the deliberate evasion on which the exchange turns.
findings.japanese: 「…好きですよ、麻理さんのこと」

findings.highlight: we're in a state where we still haven't come to the conclusion we want, and when we're just one step away from it, too
findings.evidenceJa: だって、そこに辿り着きたいという結論にすら、まだ辿り着いていないという、さらに一歩手前の状態なんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has not even reached the conclusion that he wants to arrive at those words—he is one stage earlier than that. The English instead makes the couple sound one step away from a mutually desired conclusion, reversing how far Haruki remains from commitment.
findings.japanese:
だって、そこに辿り着きたいという結論にすら、
まだ辿り着いていないという、
さらに一歩手前の状態なんだから。
findings.todokanai: After all, we're in a state where we still haven't come to the conclusion we want, and when we're just one step away from it, too.

findings.highlight: she did sound exceptionally cheerful today
findings.evidenceJa: でも今日は、いつもと比べると格段に嬉しい言葉があったから、差し引きでも大幅プラスに傾いていた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says there was something Mari said today that made him far happier than usual, enough to leave the emotional balance strongly positive. The English instead describes Mari herself as sounding exceptionally cheerful, reassigning the emotion and losing why the promised return matters to him.
findings.japanese:
でも今日は、いつもと比べると
格段に嬉しい言葉があったから、
差し引きでも大幅プラスに傾いていた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, she did sound exceptionally cheerful today, so if you consider the good and the bad, I'd say it definitely leaned toward the good.
